title: Iminodiacetic acid stabilized 3d-4f clusters: Synthesis, structure, and magnetism
claim: Packing many Gd(III) ions into one IDA 3d-Gd cluster, then encapsulating it in a biocompatible polymer, is presented as a route to stronger MRI contrast at lower dose than small-molecule Gd agents.
explanation: Multiple Gd(III) centers raise the longitudinal relaxation contribution. Polymer-encapsulated Gd52Ni56 (PEC-3) is the concrete case: it is water-soluble, forms vesicular nanostructures, and is compared in vivo with DTPA-Gd after intratumor injection.
scope: Polymer-encapsulated IDA Gd-Ni clusters as T1 MRI contrast candidates.
conditions: Biocompatible polymer encapsulation of Gd52Ni56; in vivo comparison described for PEC-3 versus DTPA-Gd.
caveats: The performance claim is tied to the PEC-3 study; the review does not provide a numerical relaxivity in the text.
